headline: A Mainframe Playground Opens Again
lede: VM/370 Community Edition brings IBM’s virtual-machine world within reach of an emulator and a 3270 terminal. The guide moves from minidisks and CMS commands to old languages, games, and the peculiar pleasures of a system built for many machines at once.

headline: A Faster Route Through Text Generation
lede: Next-Concept Modeling replaces repeated diffusion sampling with a hierarchy of coarse-to-fine codes predicted in parallel. On modest models and selected benchmarks, the paper reports substantially fewer function evaluations and faster generation, while leaving scale and generality open to question.

headline: A Local SketchUp Alternative Takes Shape
lede: KetchUp brings Rust, WebGPU, and a familiar Push/Pull workflow to an open-source 3D modeling tool. Models stay local, move through portable files, and remain useful for the practical work of planning furniture, woodworking, and other builds.

headline: A License Plate Could Open the Door
lede: A chain of exposed services, hardcoded credentials, authorization failures, and an MFA bypass turned a car’s license plate into a starting point for account takeover. The resulting tokens could unlock vehicles and start engines across multiple countries. Fix the identity stack, not just the dashboard.

headline: Nvidia Appeared in One Round in Eleven
lede: Nvidia or its venture arm joined 79 of 949 private-company funding rounds worth at least $100 million. The count makes the chipmaker a conspicuous strategic investor in the startups building around its stack.

headline: The AI Boom May Be Real—and Fragile
lede: The case against an imminent AI bubble rests on growing revenue, compute-level margins, and demand that may extend well beyond today’s infrastructure cycle. But debt, financing commitments, regulation, and uncertain pricing power leave the investment story considerably less settled than the technology story.
pullquote: Real utility does not make every AI investment a good one.

headline: Dragging Becomes a State-Transition Problem
lede: Declarative Dragging asks authors to describe the states an object may reach, then lets the system synthesize geometry, feedback, and animation. Its demos show how a model-driven approach can make intricate interactions composable rather than hand-coded one gesture at a time.

headline: Psalm 7 Makes PHP Analysis Sharper
lede: Psalm 7 folds type checking, dead-code detection, and taint analysis into one faster pass. Security tracking expands across frameworks and language features, with support for newer PHP syntax and a capability-based purity model.

headline: A Browser Learns to Sing Through Physics
lede: Chimera Vocal Synth models airflow through the throat, mouth, and nose instead of replaying recorded samples. Move the tongue, lips, and jaw, and the instrument exposes the resonances, formants, and pressure behind the sound.

headline: Outlook Raises the DMARC Gate
lede: Outlook.com is rejecting some mail from domains without a DMARC record, even when SPF and DKIM are present. For small senders, one `v=DMARC1; p=none` TXT record may be the first step toward keeping invoices, applications, and ordinary replies out of the bounce queue.
